comparison: Both evaluate LD presence and distribution in testis (C1, C10-C16) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on microscopy validation methods while peer review emphasizes the thorough and rigorous characterization. Peer R1 also includes developmental stage claims (C17-C24) that OpenEval separates into R2.

Both evaluate stage-specific LD localization (C17-C24) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes statistical methods (Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests) and correlation with developmental markers. Peer review groups these claims with basic LD characterization (C1, C10-C16) and praises the quantification as thorough and well-executed.

Both evaluate bmm expression patterns and LD accumulation in mutants (C2, C29-C39) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval separates bmm expression (R3: C2, C29-C36) from mutant phenotypes (R4: C37-C39), while peer review groups all these claims together. Both praise the quantitative validation and scRNA-seq analysis.

Both evaluate LD accumulation in bmm mutants (C37-C39) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on statistical rigor and lineage-specific confirmation. Peer review groups these with bmm expression claims (C2, C29-C36) and confirms the quantitative support for increased LDs in mutants.

Perfect agreement on cell-autonomous function (C4, C40-C44) as SUPPORTED. Both emphasize the rigor of FLP-FRT clonal analysis and stage-specific effects in spermatocytes. Peer review confirms the quantitative analysis clearly supports cell-autonomous role, and editor summary highlights this as convincing data.

Both evaluate spermatogenic defects (C3, C45-C50) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes temperature sensitivity and temporal persistence with appropriate statistics. Peer review emphasizes beautiful images with rigorous quantification and confirms testis size and spermatid number defects.

Both evaluate conservation and dietary rescue (C51-C53) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes partial rescue suggests additional mechanisms. Peer review groups these with spermatogenic defects (C3, C45-C50) and states the data support broad significance across phyla as a key strength.

Both evaluate GSC and hub phenotypes (C54-C60) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes multiple approaches distinguishing cell-autonomous from non-cell-autonomous effects. Peer review confirms clonal data are convincing with minor caveat that hub enlargement may explain GSC number increase.

Both evaluate differentiation defects (C61-C67) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights convergence of multiple phenotypic markers with appropriate statistics. Peer review groups these with GSC/hub phenotypes (C54-C60, C68-C73) and confirms the quantitative support.

Both evaluate germline clonal analysis (C68-C69, C72) with caution. OpenEval designates UNCERTAIN due to marginal significance (p=0.0496) and authors' own caveat. Peer review designates SUPPORTED but explicitly acknowledges the p-value is less robust and may reflect low sample size.

OpenEval evaluates somatic clone findings (C70-C71, C73) as UNCERTAIN, noting speculative interpretation of non-cell-autonomous function without direct testing. Peer review groups these with other clonal analyses (C54-C73) and designates SUPPORTED, though focuses more on germline findings in evaluation text.

Both evaluate lipidomic profiling (C5, C77-C84) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes comprehensive methodology with 293 lipid species identified and statistical enrichment of triglycerides. Peer review praises rigorous profiling and notes the data will be useful to researchers studying lipid species.

Both evaluate substrate specificity analysis (C85-C88) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights highly significant correlation statistics and alignment with known ATGL preferences. Peer review groups these with broader lipidomic findings (C5, C77-C89) and confirms triglycerides are most affected by bmm loss.

Both evaluate additional lipidomic changes (C89) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these are secondary findings representing comprehensive characterization. Peer review groups with all lipidomic data (C5, C77-C89) in thorough analysis of triglycerides as important LD component.

Both evaluate genetic epistasis with mdy (C6, C93-C97) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes rigorous genetic approach testing causality with rescue of multiple phenotypes. Peer review confirms double mutant reverts bmm phenotypes, consistent with the model, and notes statistically significant tissue-specific rescue.

Both evaluate germline-specific rescue (C98-C100) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes partial rescue and need for additional experiments on spermatid defects. Peer review confirms tissue-specific rescue of testis size phenotype is supported by statistically significant quantitation.

Both evaluate main conclusions integrating multiple evidence lines (C7-C9, C90, C97, C101) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes convergence of genetic, lipidomic, and phenotypic data. Peer review confirms convincing data that triglyceride lipase is required cell-autonomously and that triglyceride increase is detrimental to spermatogenesis.

OpenEval evaluates background literature claims (C25-C28, C74-C76) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these represent established context rather than novel findings requiring peer assessment.

OpenEval evaluates background knowledge claims (C102-C111) as SUPPORTED with extensive literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these provide field context and are not novel experimental findings.

OpenEval evaluates background and knowledge gaps (C112-C127) as SUPPORTED, establishing study rationale. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these motivational claims are not experimental results requiring peer validation.
